At least, that’s true when it comes to his early investment in Anthropic AI, the artificial intelligence company that saw major financial wins this week when it went public and sold $81.3 billion worth of stock shares, according to CNBC .

Noting he's “happy" about the company's recent successes, Thompson told Yahoo Finance that he got involved in the tech brand over two years ago while visiting San Francisco as part of his NBA schedule when he was playing for the Cleveland Cavaliers.

Thompson—who shares kids True , 8, and Tatum , 4, with ex Khloe Kardashian —met up with Sriram Krishnan , now a Senior White House Policy Advisor on Artificial Intelligence, who he described as a "great buddy of mine."

"The only friend that I had in SF during those Finals runs that was picking the Cavaliers to win, he opened up these doors," Thompson recalled in the interview published Nov. 19. "Going to dinners and and meeting people. I think SF is one of those towns where a lot of great founders and early startups, they want to come together and build this ecosystem."

"And I said, 'You know what? Let me insert myself in,'" the 35-year-old said. "I'm the tall guy walking in. I'm probably about 10 inches taller than everyone else, and [say], 'Tell me what you're working on.'"

Now, years after becoming an investor, Thompson explained how thrilled they were last month when Anthropic announced it had filed a proposed stock plan with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

"We're in a group chat and everyone's just talking about what they're going to do to celebrate," Thompson shared. "I said, 'Guys, the one thing we have to do is do a dinner. We got to break bread again.'"

Because, as the Miami Heat player admitted, his ventures don't always pay off like Anthropic did, breaking records with its initial public offering ( CNBC reported it had a fully diluted market cap of about $1.8 trillion on Nov. 19).

entertainment.title: Rising Argentine Star Milo J Signs With CAA
entertainment.summary: The rapper, singer, producer and songwriter recently took home four Latin Grammys and is up for two Grammys in 2027.
entertainment.body:
Argentinian rapper, singer, producer and songwriter Milo J signed with CAA, the agency announced Friday (Nov. 20).

The 20-year-old artist launched his career in 2021 as part of the Buenos Aires-based indie artist collective BajoWest and gained attention via YouTube and TikTok. In 2023, he received his first Latin Grammy nomination in the best rap/hip-hop category. That same year, he released his debut studio album 111 , which featured Peso Pluma, Yahritza y Su Esencia, Nicki Nicole and Yami Safdie. He later signed with Sony Music Latin.

In September, Milo released his third studio album, La Vide Era Más Corta . In the wake of that release, which blended traditional Argentine folkloric influences into his sound, he began playing arenas and stadiums in Spanish-speaking markets. Earlier this year, he took home 13 trophies at Premios Gardel — Argentina’s equivalent of the Grammys — including artist of the year. He won four Latin Grammys at this year’s ceremony, including record of the year, and has been nominated for two 2027 Grammys, including best Latin song (“Niño”) and best Latin rock/alternative album ( La Vida Era Más Corta ).

Among other recent milestones, Milo recently performed on The Tonight Show With Jimmy Fallon . He’s slated to perform at a crop of upcoming events including Vive Latino, Coachella, Isle of Light, Panama Crossroads and Estéreo Picnic. He’ll also soon headline his first shows in Brazil, including at the Rock in Rio festival, as well as shows across Central America at 7,000-17,000-capacity venues and at a stadium in Córdoba, Argentina.

entertainment.title: Vanity Fair editor defends cover profile with terse Timothée Chalamet: ‘He was a lovely houseguest’
entertainment.summary: Vanity Fair's feature on Chalamet was panned for featuring more interesting details about Mark Guiducci's apartment decor than juicy quotes from the actor.
entertainment.body:
It read like an article from Architectural Digest rather than Vanity Fair.

Online gadflies scorned VF Global Editorial Director Mark Guiducci after his cover feature on Timothée Chalamet featured more interesting details about his own apartment decor than juicy quotes from the “Dune: Part Three” star.

Condé Nast’s buzzy celebrity title had scored the chance to shoot the fashion-forward actor for the cover of its holiday issue, and whipped up an arresting Aidan Zamiri photo portfolio of the actor screaming among waterfalls in Iceland.

But, as often happens with big celebrities with powerful gatekeepers these days, the access provided for the interview produced content of a far less thrilling nature. Chalamet asked that Guiducci, who is not normally a writer, pen the cover feature himself — and the agreed-upon setting for their mere 90-minute conversation was … Guiducci’s own one-bedroom apartment in the East 60s.

“He can’t go many places in public,” Guiducci told Page Six, explaining the unusual choice of venue. “So I thought it would be good to meet him halfway. I thought that if I revealed a little bit of myself, he might reveal a little bit of himself.”

The hoped-for revelations didn’t seem to come, however: A taciturn Timmy showed up with a Lenwich Italiano sandwich in a paper bag and proceeded to give the dapper editor very little in the way of material. Throughout the story, the “Wonka” star offers responses like “Okay, pass” and “I’m going to pull a Frank Ocean and be mysterious” rather than answer simple questions.

In his editor’s letter in the issue, Guiducci compared Chalamet , who is dating one of the most photographed women in the world, Kylie Jenner, to mega-movie stars Marlon Brando and Leonardo DiCaprio.

“With each of these stars, one rule usually holds true,” Guiducci wrote. “The bigger they get, the less they open their mouth.”

Nguyen Quynh Anh 's reign as Miss Universe Vietnam has officially come to an end.

The beauty queen was initially suspended in October when private messages speaking negatively about other pageant participants became public, and now the organizers have revoked her title due to Nguyen's conduct while under suspension.

The issues occurred while Nguyen was barred from performing in all "artistic performance activities" related to Miss Universe for six months, the show’s organizers, Five6 Entertainment, announced in a Nov. 18 statement , according to Tuoi Tre News .

In addition to being suspended from events for the group text—which included runner-up Trinh My Anh —containing derogatory remarks about past winners, fellow contestants and judges, the model was ordered to pay a fine, the outlet said.

However, when the influencer attended a community event while banned from representing the pageant, the production company, per Tuoi Tre News, said her appearance caused issues that "affected the image of Miss Universe Vietnam and its organizers."

In addition to promoting her title while suspended, the organizers stated that the 27-year-old delayed signing her management contract in order to prioritize a "mental health condition" amid the transitional period. Still, the team said they learned Nguyen signed an exclusive contract with a competitor management agency and "continued accepting performance engagements and attending events without reaching an agreement with Five6."

In response to the initial backlash, the competition's runner-up, Trinh, apologized on Instagram . Meanwhile, Nguyen released an Oct. 13 statement transcribed by the outlet where she apologized "to the women concerned and everyone affected by this incident, especially the audience."

"I understand that holding a beauty queen title does not make me incapable of making mistakes," her statement continued. "However, the title requires me to be more mindful and careful about my words, conduct and responsibilities, even in seemingly minor matters."

entertainment.title: Leonard Nimoy's TV Debut Was On A Drama Directed By The Legendary Blake Edwards
entertainment.summary: Leonard Nimoy was in danger of forever being typecast when he worked with Blake Edwards, but instead, his career trajectory took him to the director's realm.
entertainment.body:
The series takes its name from four major stars of the era: Charles Boyer, David Niven, Dick Powell, and Ida Lupino. However, none of them are featured in this episode. Written and directed by Blake Edwards, who'd later become famous for creating "The Pink Panther" movies and directing "Breakfast at Tiffany's," this story is all about boxing. Bulloti is frequently chewing a cigar, a typical baddie who makes money from rigging matches. With his big fedora, Nimoy looks like a classic gangster. Although he has a couple of lines while hanging around with his boss, most of the time, he's simply an imposing background character.

This gig was emblematic of Nimoy's early career. "The roles that I was being cast in were always offbeat, nasty guys," he explained to The Television Academy in 2000. "I became useful eventually playing heavies." While he didn't have a look that aligned with the stereotypical leading man of that era, in the mid-1960s, this legendary actor would really shake up cultural expectations with his portrayal of Spock on "Star Trek."

Although these two legends never worked together again, Nimoy did follow in Edwards' footsteps and become a respected director, starting with an episode of Rod Serling's "Night Gallery." Surprisingly, in the early 1960s, when people first started encouraging him to try directing, he wasn't receptive. "I was insulted," Nimoy admitted to The Nacelle Company . "I thought, 'Are these people telling me there's something wrong with my acting?'" Fortunately, he later realized this wasn't a mutually exclusive decision, and he made the most of his skills by directing and starring in "Star Trek III: The Search for Spock" and "Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home."

With its funny moments, like the classic bus scene where Spock neck pinches a punk and shuts off a loud boombox, "The Voyage Home" reignited Nimoy's zest for comedy, one of Edwards' particular specialties. As a director, Edwards was a master at making decisions to heighten the hilarity of a scene, with strategic pauses and shot framing that led to unexpected, funny consequences. While Nimoy felt his professional reputation as stoic Spock might have caused him to be viewed as a strictly serious guy, after he directed 1987's "Three Men and a Baby," he cemented his reputation as a comedic director.

entertainment.summary: The Scorsese favorite has shared scenes with Leonardo DiCaprio and Margot Robbie. Now he's playing Irwin Winkler, the producing legend behind 'Rocky' and 'Goodfellas.'
entertainment.body:
Logo text Ever since P.J. Byrne had a literal meltdown in the most showstopping scene of Damien Chazelle ’s Babylon , his career as a scene-stealing character actor has reached a new high.

The New Jersey native’s 2026 alone has brought eight credits, including the conclusion of his recurring character on The Boys , Coyote vs. Acme , The End of Oak Street and a series-regular role on USA’s basic cable hit The Rainmaker . Most notably, he now stars in his biggest film role to date as Oscar-winning Rocky producer Irwin Winkler in Peter Farrelly ’s biographical awards contender, I Play Rocky . Related Stories Hollywood Flashback Yo, Academy! When 'Rocky' Was Crowned Best Picture Champ Movies 'Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' Hunts Down $21M in Box Office Previews

In 1975, Winkler and his producing partner Robert Chartoff were developing Martin Scorsese ’s New York, New York at the same time as the underdog story from a then-unknown Sylvester Stallone . The former would become the first of a half-dozen films Winkler collaborated on with Scorsese, including 2013’s The Wolf of Wall Street . It’s fitting, then, that Byrne is now playing the celebrated producer, given that his own career turning point came with his role as Rugrat in Scorsese and Leonardo DiCaprio’s unhinged take on the life of former stockbroker Jordan Belfort. (Byrne would later reunite with Scorsese on his 2016 series Vinyl .)

Byrne’s turn as a founding member of Belfort’s Stratton Oakmont is probably best remembered for one particularly rambunctious trading-floor scene in which his character shaves a female sales assistant’s head. The opportunity also allowed Byrne to put his unused finance degree from Boston College to work, albeit in a fictionalized version of a career path he had quickly abandoned because of his aversion to boiler-room culture.

In the mid-’90s, one of his Boston College professors encouraged him to try his hand at drama school instead, leading him to DePaul University in Chicago. Byrne’s time in the Windy City seems to have left a lasting impression. He often speaks about acting in the same terms that Chicago Bulls legend Michael Jordan once used to describe his record-setting 3-point barrage against the Portland Trail Blazers in Game 1 of the 1992 NBA Finals. When Byrne acts, he strives to enter a flow state, or “the zone,” as Jordan called it, where he’s so locked in to the task at hand that distractions fade and he can achieve peak performance.

entertainment.title: Sarah Michelle Gellar Reveals Surprising Freddie Prinze Jr. Connection
entertainment.summary: Now this is a revelation to wig out over. Sarah Michelle Gellar and Freddie Prinze Jr.’s paths didn’t officially cross until the late ‘90s on I Know What You Did Last Summer, but as they recently...
entertainment.body:
Sarah Michelle Gellar and Freddie Prinze Jr. ’s paths didn’t officially cross until the late ‘90s on I Know What You Did Last Summer , but as they recently learned they had more in common than they realized. Specifically, a shared family experience that traces back decades before they graced the screen.

“We always joke that the closest connection I had to my husband's side of the family,” Gellar told E! News in an exclusive interview, “was that for a small time I went to the same high school that my husband's dad went to, and that was like sort of our one thing.”

After all, though Gellar— mom to Charlotte , 17, and Rocky , 14 , with Prinze—is a native New Yorker, her husband was born in Los Angeles and grew up in New Mexico. (His dad Freddie Prinze , however, hailed from New York.)

She continued, “Then through Ancestry, we found out that our grandparents lived less than two miles away from each other in the Bronx at one point, which they could have potentially known each other. That's kind of crazy.”

For the Buffy the Vampire Slayer star , who teamed up with Ancestry for its Gathering the Good initiative, it was an opportunity to explore her own family’s legacy while also looking at the spirit of giving through history. So, tracing how her loved ones made the journey to America in the 1890s at the same time philanthropist Lena Sittig space was creating what is now considered to be the modern toy drive, really hit home how interconnected the mission is.

“I learned that my grandmother was coming over on a ship at 16 years old, right when Lena was having her idea for this,” she shared. “It’s kind of crazy how the world intertwines, and it just reminds you that you're just such a small part of such a bigger picture.”

It’s especially poignant as diving back into her roots has not always been a focal point for Gellar.

“It's funny, I didn't really spend that much time thinking about my history and my ancestry because I try so hard to live in the moment,” she explained. “And when Ancestry came to me and talked about what they wanted to do, I thought, ‘What a great idea to be able to learn acts of kindness, acts of goodness that your family may have been a part of that you never knew.’”

entertainment.title: Watch Ice Spice’s Speechless Reaction to Seeing Her Madame Tussauds Wax Figure for the First Time: ‘This Is So Accurate’
entertainment.summary: The figurine took it back to 2023 with her signature cropped orange curls.
entertainment.body:
Ice Spice got the wax-figure treatment at Madame Tussauds New York on Thursday (Nov. 19), and the Bronx rapper was gagged at seeing her waxy twin for the first time — to the point where she was a little spooked at how the artists nailed her look, leaving her briefly speechless.

The look sported by Ice’s figurine takes fans back to 2022 and 2023, when she was rising star working her way up the rap ranks with her signature copper curls.

She’s rocking a red tiger catsuit, which was donated from the “Deli” rapper’s wardrobe, along with Black Air Jordan 4s, a replica of the diamond-encrused bracelet gifted to her by Doja Cat and her Icy Princess pendant chain.

“It’s so accurate. I have a really unique face and I’m impressed they got it so right,” she said before later joking, “This is so accurate, like oh my God, my big-ass forehead, you literally got it.”

The 26-year-old posted a series of photos alongside her wax sister to social media on Friday (Nov. 20). “Put it on wax ;),” she wrote in her caption.

The Ice Spice wax figure will be on display at the Times Square location of Madame Tussauds New York in the heart of NYC into 2027.

“Ice Spice is a defining part of New York’s music and culture scene, so bringing her into Madame Tussauds New York feels especially meaningful,” said Tiago Mogadouro, who serves as the general manager for Madame Tussauds New York. “She represents a new generation of artists who are shaping the city’s identity in real time, and we’re excited to give fans a way to celebrate that right here in Times Square.”

entertainment.title: ‘Brady Bunch’ actress Eve Plumb warns aspiring young actors they ‘don’t want to be famous’
entertainment.summary: "The Brady Bunch" aired for five seasons on ABC between 1969 and 1974.
entertainment.body:
Eve Plumb, best known for portraying Jan Brady on “The Brady Bunch,” is cautioning aspiring young actors against pursuing fame.

During the Nov. 14 episode of the “Facts Verse” podcast , the actress said she is regularly approached by children who tell her they “want to be famous.”

“No, you don’t want to be famous,” Plumb, 68, said. “If you want to be an actor and you want to do good work, you want to play interesting parts, sure, but you don’t want to be famous.”

She went on to explain that her pushback against that desire for stardom stems from the fact that “once you’re famous, you can’t go back.”

“People will always know you for whatever it is that you’ve done, whether it’s good or bad, so you don’t really want to be famous,” she added.

Plumb shared similar sentiments in a May interview with Fox News Digital , noting that “the power to say ‘no’ is very valuable as an actor.”

“We always talk about setting boundaries, and my parents always made sure that I had time off and that I did the right things,” she told the outlet. “You don’t have to say ‘yes’ to everything. And I am still that way today.”

Plumb also shared what she hopes for other child actors following in her footsteps.

entertainment.summary: The actor died on Nov. 10 at the age of 62.
entertainment.body:
Comedian Anthony Clark’s cause of death has been revealed as septic shock after his death on Nov. 10 at age 62.

Influenza A and chronic alcoholism were listed as underlying conditions, according to the death certificate obtained by People Friday. Acute kidney failure was listed as a contributing factor.

Clark’s former “Yes, Dear” co-star Mike O’Malley announced Wednesday on X that he passed away, recalling his last phone call with the actor in an emotional tribute.

O’Malley remembered Clark as a “hilarious guy,” and reminisced about seeing him perform at The Comedy Connection in Boston with his wife, Lisa, in the mid-’90s.

“…We laughed and laughed and laughed. He was so unique — one of those comics who is laughing along with you at the absurdity of his stories and observations,” O’Malley wrote.

“I was a fan before I was a friend. We spoke on the phone three weeks ago. He had us laughing loudly once again,” he wrote.

In his message, he included photos from their last episode of “Yes, Dear,” which aired in 2006. O’Malley also posted a similar message to his Instagram page.

Clark was best known for his role as Greg Warner in the hit CBS sitcom about two married couples — whose wives are sisters — living under the same roof.

entertainment.summary: Linda Cardellini shared the screen with several future Hollywood stars in a beloved late-'90s dramedy. Now, the cult classic is available to watch for free.
entertainment.body:
Created by Paul Feig, the series follows siblings Lindsay Weir (Cardellini) and Sam Weir (John Francis Daley) as they navigate different social circles at their high school in the early '80s. In addition to Cardellini, the cast included James Franco, Seth Rogen, Jason Segel, Martin Starr, and Busy Philipps, all of whom went on to successful careers in Hollywood.

Although "Freaks and Geeks" aired on NBC for only one season (1999-2000), it has since become a cult classic and one of the best coming-of-age shows of all time . "It's everything you hope will happen when you create something that usually is more of a movie," Feig told Collider in June 2021. "I guess it's TV, too. You always just hope whatever you do is going to have a longevity, and that people will like to keep watching it and new people will find it as the years go by." He continued, "But it really happens so rarely."

If you're hoping for new episodes, however, you're out of luck, at least for now. That said, Linda Cardellini hasn't ruled out returning for a reboot. "You can never say never," she told Us Weekly in May 2019. "You know, if everybody was on board and ... everybody came up with a great idea." She continued, "But I don't know how they would do it."

Meanwhile, Seth Rogen, who played Ken Miller, would rather leave the past in the past. Speaking to People in February 2023, he addressed the possibility of a revival. "I don't think anyone would do it," he said, adding, "It's so rare that you do something in your career that is actually just viewed as good." He continued, "I know enough now not to f*** with that, to just let it be good and not try to go revisit it."

entertainment.summary: Golloria can’t conceal her thoughts on Huda Beauty’s apology. After the makeup brand’s founder Huda Kattan apologized to the beauty influencer for how her company handled discontinuing their...
entertainment.body:
Golloria can’t conceal her thoughts on Huda Beauty’s apology.

After the makeup brand’s founder Huda Kattan apologized to the beauty influencer for how her company handled discontinuing their darkest setting powder Coffee Cake and replacing it with Coco Truffle, Golloria shared her thoughts on the response.

“I appreciate your apology and you taking the time to get back to me,” Golloria posted in the comments of Kattan’s Nov. 20 Instagram post . “Speaking from both my experience as a shade consultant and as a dark skinned woman whose shade options are directly affected by this decision, I don’t think Coco Truffle should replace Coffee Cake. And that’s just the honest truth.”

The TikToker explained that she heard Huda Beauty’s reasoning that Coffee Cake wasn’t doing well with consumers, but added that she didn’t think the two shades were “interchangeable,” noting that “a shade occupying a similar depth in a range doesn’t necessarily mean it serves the same complexions.”

“You’ve said several times that you want to better serve dark skinned women, and part of that is listening to the women telling you that Coffee Cake already works for them,” the 25-year-old continued. “That feedback should help guide what you preserve as you expand the range.”

She also added that darker skinned women “deserve variety in both depth and undertone,” and that having both shades would help create that inclusion. Instead, Golloria shared in her own Instagram caption that she felt Huda Beauty was “doing what's easiest for the brand instead of what's needed by the women you say you want to serve.”

“Inclusion means making room for our differences,” she wrote, “not asking us to settle for whatever is most convenient for you to offer.”

As for Kattan, while the beauty founder did not reply to Golloria’s comment, she explained in her apology video that she was sorry for how the conversation about the shade replacement had been handled with Golloria, especially as it was happening during a busy time for the brand and when Kattan herself had to undergo emergency surgery for a ruptured breast implant in April.

entertainment.title: Percy Jackson EPs Break Down Percy And Annabeth's First Dance, Explain How Season 3 Honors The Duo's 'Connection'
entertainment.summary: The team behind Percy Jackson and the Olympians discusses that big premiere moment for Percy and Annabeth - one of their few scenes together in Season 3.
entertainment.body:
The first two episodes of "Percy Jackson and the Olympians" Season 3 are now streaming on Disney+, and what better way to celebrate than with a party? A school dance, perhaps?

Yes, the Season 3 premiere sends Percy (Walker Scobell), Annabeth ( Leah Sava' Jeffries ), and Thalia (Tamara Smart) to Westover Hall, a military boarding school where they're meant to recruit a pair of demigod siblings to their cause. And wouldn't you know it, the trio just happens to arrive on the night of the school's winter dance.

This results in a moment that #Percabeth shippers will undoubtedly revisit for years to come — Percy and Annabeth 's first dance together. With Billy Joel's "She's Always a Woman" playing from the speakers, the best friends bring their complicated feelings onto the dance floor, putting a spotlight on their developing relationship in more ways than one.

So, what made this the perfect soundtrack for Percy and Annabeth's first dance? "As Mrs. Gottschalk says, she's slowing it down at 3/4 time, so we wanted something that timeless and brought everybody to that space," co-showrunner John Steinberg tells TVLine. "You feel the dreaded shift from fast-dance song to slow-dance song. It does feel like the perfect song to shift into like, wait a minute, what's about to happen here?"

The premiere, and this dance in particular, does a lot of heavy lifting, as it's one of the few moments Percy and Annabeth get to share together before they're separated.

"Because this season is so about them being separated, this first episode needed to kind of set up where they are with each other and the connection that they have," Steinberg adds. "Because pretty much the rest of the season is both of them fighting to get back to each other."

Disney+ As the series progresses, and as its main characters grow into young adults, it's becoming harder for "Percy Jackson and the Olympians" to ignore what's brewing between besties Percy and Annabeth. This presents an interesting challenge to the show's producing team — how do they explore what we all know is coming without getting too ahead of themselves? Not unlike Percy and Annabeth at the winter formal, the process of writing their story is a delicate dance.

"I feel like there are a lot of fans who read into any moment," co-showrunner Craig Silverstein tells TVLine. "We might think we're taking it slowly, but they're taking it and boosting it up, so I'm not even sure if our intention matters because people are going to find that."

Although the shows are quite different, arguably the biggest change was visual.

Rather than shooting with multiple cameras in front of a live studio audience, as was the case with its predecessor, "Young Sheldon" was a single-camera sitcom from the get-go. "It's more intimate," co-creator Chuck Lorre once explained when speaking with Channel 4 . "The pacing, obviously, is very different. The actors aren't having to hold for laughs. They're not playing to the proscenium." For Lorre and co-creator Steven Molaro, it was important to allow the family drama to breathe.

"We knew going in that we were going to be working with a cast of young children," Lorre continued, "and it seemed like the more appropriate way for them to get the best work, to do the best work, was in a closed setting where they had the time to develop these characters." The result changed the tone from the classic laugh-track style to more of a family-oriented dramedy that had the chance to convey deeper, more heartfelt moments.

CBS The prequel stood largely on its own, even to the point that "Young Sheldon" often rewrote "The Big Bang Theory" canon . Spanning seven seasons on the network, the program ended with a four-year audience high that raked in around half the audience its predecessor's conclusion did. Nevertheless, "Young Sheldon" was a feat to be celebrated by Lorre and Molaro, marking the former's first single-camera sitcom.

"It's a wholly different way to tell a story, and the working process is very different," Lorre explained concerning the transition from multi-cam to single-cam. "It's much slower, you know. But the end result is something to be proud of, really." When recalling the Cooper family dinner scene from the pilot, Molaro added: "In the time it took us to shoot that, we could have shot two episodes of 'Big Bang Theory' in front of an audience."

"Young Sheldon" was popular enough that the "Big Bang" universe continued to expand with "Georgie & Mandy's First Marriage" in 2024. The spin-off returned to the multi-camera, live studio audience set up, with the pilot jokingly speaking to the merits of a laugh track. "Some shows you can hear people laughing, and some you can't," Sheldon's brother Georgie (Montana Jordan) explains. In 2026, "Big Bang" expanded again with another single-cam spin-off, "Stuart Fails to Save the Universe," which featured a nod to its multi-cam roots in its mind-bending Season 1 finale .

entertainment.body:
Logo text In late January, Amazon ‘s Brett Ratner -directed Melania documentary debuted at the Kennedy Center in Washington amid crowds of demonstrators in the wake of the fatal shootings by ICE agents of Alex Pretti and Renée Good in Minneapolis. The president had also sparked backlash for his efforts to overhaul the Kennedy Center, including adding his name to the exterior, which are still playing out in court.

Thursday night, Melania: The Series , a two-episode follow-up, though part of the initial $40 million project, consisting of bonus footage, debuted at New York’s Lincoln Center. Those involved with the film and series downplayed any significance of the change in venue, noting the president and first lady’s ties to New York. But if there were demonstrators, they weren’t seen or heard by those inside the tight-security screening at Alice Tully Hall, though whether that’s due to people moving on or the premiere location remains an open question. The screening came just two weeks after the 2026 midterm elections saw Democrats score historic, surprise victories in a referendum on the president that will result in a change in party control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate.

Still, Trump’s longtime adviser Marc Beckman previously teased that the docuseries , now streaming on Amazon’s Prime Video , would be a “total different experience, completely new.”

Speaking to The Hollywood Reporter ahead of the Melania: The Series premiere, Beckman explained how the filmmaking team determined what would go in the documentary and what would be for the series.

“We decided that we would bifurcate and isolate certain stories that we thought were suitable for the series that weren’t necessarily appropriate for the film,” Beckman said. “The reason they’re suitable for the series is because it gives us more time to unpack more of her storyline, more about her family, more about her career, more about philanthropy and also what happens right after the inauguration when she takes on the role of being first lady of the United States again.”

Melania: The Series producer Fernando Sulichin, who took on the same role on the documentary, added that the film “was about going into the inauguration, and this one is first lady in action and what she’s about, more intimate — not the preparation of becoming the first lady but being the first lady.”

Scheana Shay revealed she doesn’t want her daughter to be “alone” in the event of a loved one’s death.

The reality star and Davies, 36, welcomed Summer in April 2021, sharing the news in an emotional social media post.

“My heart is SO FULL 🤍 On the morning of 4/26/21 we welcomed to the world Summer Moon Honey Davies, weighing in at 6lbs 12 oz,” Shay wrote via Instagram at the time.

entertainment.title: This Dark Comedy Series From The Writers Of Deadpool Is Perfect For A Weekend Binge
entertainment.summary: The minds behind "Deadpool" also executive produced a totally underrated dark comedy TV series that, if you love "Deadpool," is the perfect weekend binge.
entertainment.body:
YouTube Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover With only 10 episodes and an endearing vigilante protagonist, "Wayne" is the perfect bite-sized watch for "Deadpool" fans on the go.

Released to YouTube Premium in 2019, "Wayne" is an action comedy series that boasts executive producing and writing credits from both Rhett Reese and Paul Wernick, the infamous writing team behind the "Deadpool" film franchise. The universally acclaimed show follows the misadventures of Wayne McCullough (Mark McKenna,) a jaded Massachusetts teenager who tends to solve his problems with his fists. After Wayne develops feelings for a sarcastic girl named Del, he joins forces with her to track down the 1979 Pontiac Trans Am that was stolen from his late father.

Like "Deadpool," "Wayne" doesn't shy away from gore or violence — but, just like its titular character, its rugged exterior hides a secret, irresistible sweetness. Reviewers have consistently praised "Wayne" for its careful development of its lovingly rough-and-tumble leads, prompting comparisons to other character-driven black comedies like Netflix's "The End of the F***ing World." Despite its widespread critical success, "Wayne" was canceled by YouTube Premium after a single season. The series resided on Amazon Prime Video from 2020 to 2023, when it was removed from the platform; as of October 12, 2026, it is available for streaming on Netflix.

YouTube When "Deadpool" writers Rhett Reese and Paul Wernick first heard about the pilot for the gritty teen rom-com that eventually became "Wayne," they were immediately onboard. "It always appeals to us, something that's not your traditional affair," Wernick confirmed in a 2019 interview with SlashFilm , reflecting on the unique "John Wick meets John Hughes" label that he and his writing partner ascribe to "Wayne."

According to Wernick, he and Reese typically gravitate to projects that play fast and loose with tone: A penchant that led them not only to "Wayne," but also to screenplays like "Zombieland" and "Deadpool." "We always say extraordinary circumstances in an ordinary world is something that appeals to us," Wernick continued. "['Wayne'] obviously I think falls into that, especially with the mixing of tone. We want you not only to laugh. We think of this as a comedy but we also think of this as many other things: action adventure, it's a road trip and has an emotional story, a love story between two kids who are coming of age."

sports.title: Brock Bowers doesn't know whether he will play Sunday
sports.summary: Raiders tight end Brock Bowers is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Broncos.
sports.body:
Bowers didn’t practice Wednesday but was limited Thursday and Friday. He said he was “feeling all right,” but can’t say whether he will play.

“I don’t know. We still have some conversations to have,” Bowers said.

Bowers injured his right ankle on the opening drive of the Raiders’ 21-13 loss to the Seahawks. He tried to play through it before leaving for good.

Bowers played 11 snaps, and he caught two passes for 18 yards.

“I really wanted to play, so I was just doing everything I could to get back out there, like just trying a new tape job and stuff,” Bowers said. “Felt it each time I went back out there. It was tough.”

Bowers has 50 catches for 676 yards and six touchdowns this season.

sports.title: Colts officially place Daniel Jones on waivers
sports.summary: Daniel Jones is officially on the waiver wire.
sports.body:
The NFL transaction report has gone out this afternoon, and Jones appears as a waiver from the Colts. After the trade deadline, every player who gets released by his team has to go on waivers before he becomes a free agent.

That means any team that wants Jones on his current contract can claim him, but that is extraordinarily unlikely to happen. As the waiver transaction notes, Jones is a vested veteran with a fully guaranteed salary for the rest of this season. No team is going to want to claim that salary.

Once he clears waivers, however, he’ll be an unrestricted free agent, free to sign with any team, and it won’t be surprising if some team wants to add him for veteran depth. Jones has been terrible this season, but he’s been a competent starter at times in his career, and a team that wants an experienced backup may be interested in signing him for a minimal salary.

Jones was also waived almost exactly two years ago, on November 22, 2024. He cleared waivers and signed with the Vikings’ practice squad before signing with the Colts after that season.

sports.title: NFL will consider requiring minimum-night stays for international games
sports.summary: After the 49ers and the Rams took dramatically different approaches to their arrival in Melbourne for the first-ever Australia game, we raised the question of whether the league should require teams to get there early enough to advance the goal of promoting American football to international audienc
sports.body:
Via The Athletic , the NFL will consider adopting a minimum-night stay for teams playing internationally.

“Currently, we leave those football decisions on when the team arrives in the market to the club,” NFL executive V.P. of club business, major events, and international Peter O’Reilly told The Athletic . “It is something that we’ll consider moving forward on: Do we put some minimum nights in a market in there? It’s something we’ll look at.”

The league already does it for the Super Bowl, mandating a full-week experience that includes multiple press conferences, the annual “Opening Night” media extravaganza, and practicing at designated facilities.

“Having access to players and that type of experience when they’re in the market does have a lasting impact,” O’Reilly said. “That’s a factor when you start to think about encouraging or potentially looking at a policy where you’d want a club in the market for more than the day before.”

Beyond impacting strategic considerations, it would add to the total expense. The money would be worth it, if it further enhances the league’s overall reason for going global.

sports.title: Saints officially waive S Justin Reid
sports.summary: Safety Justin Reid already penned his good-bye missive to the Saints, but his departure did not become official until 4 p.m.
sports.body:
The Saints waived Reid on Friday, with the move made official on the NFL’s personnel notice.

Reid asked for his release this week, and the Saints have granted it.

“In life and sports, things don’t always go the way you planned or hoped they would,” Reid wrote on social media. “Unfortunately, this is one of those moments . But that doesn’t change the love and respect I have for this organization or city. I truly want to see this team and this city thrive. No one deserves it more than New Orleans and the Saints.”

He will go through waivers, with the NFL announcing at 4 p.m. ET on Monday whether he clears. If no team claims him, Reid will become a free agent.

Reid joined the Saints as a free agent in 2025, and he started all 24 games he played for the team. He had 118 tackles, an interception and a half-sack.

The Jets potentially face a similar dilemma in the slot this week, albeit on offense. Both Omar Cooper and Isaiah Williams have been unable to practice, so if neither can go on Sunday, the Jets will have to make a change. One option could be to go with the guys currently on the roster. You could reactivate Jelani Woods and Tim Patrick and either run more multiple tight end packages, or use players like Garrett Wilson there. Another option could be to bring up Sterling Shepard or Jamaal Pritchett from the practice squad. The job share at running back remains a work in progress The Jets are still trying to figure out how to get the best out of Braelon Allen and Breece Hall now that both are healthy at the same time. However, Hall brings different things to the table in the passing game, so the Jets will want him on the field more often than not. Last week was interesting because they employed Hall more in the passing game in the first half with Allen getting more carries. At the half, Allen had six carries and Hall had just two. However, after halftime, Allen carried the ball just twice and Hall had nine carries. It’s possible the Jets’ thinking was that Hall might produce better after halftime if he was fresh and the defense was tired. In the end, the pair had similar rushing numbers, but Hall produced more as a receiver. “The offense will be the offense they run, but it will be centered around the quarterback, for sure,” Harbaugh said. “And they’re probably different styles to some degree, so we’ll have to look at that when the time comes. We have people doing that this week. They’ll have to make a left turn, obviously. Thanks for the info.”

Richardson is a great athlete with a big arm, and the Colts loved him coming out of Florida, and he’ll now have until the end of the season to show whether he can in any way resemble the quarterback the Colts thought they were getting when they took him fourth overall in the 2023 NFL draft. Doubtful * TE Dalton Kincaid I would just read this as “Kincaid won’t play Sunday.” Now, I know, I said the same thing about Spencer Brown last week and he suited up and made a liar out of me. Sanders This is where that “maybe three” in the section above came from. If Hawes, who is dealing with some shoulder pain, is a go, that gives them plenty of reason to sit Kincaid. The surprise here is Hamlin. The safety showed up in a walking boot and on a scooter for Wednesday’s walkthrough. Then he was listed as a DNP on Thursday. Today, he was seen running. He’s definitely trying to prove his worth to a team that keeps adding and subtracting defensive backs around him. What we’re thinking I still think this could be the week we see Tre’Davious White. Plus, it’s probably a good game to test White’s legs and see what he still has left in the tank. I’m also leading toward Shaq Thompson as well. The Bills don’t have a tight end on the practice squad, so the only other need this week is defensive secondary. Give the veterans some time – and some money – and test their game speed before the brutal Weeks 12 – 16 schedule hits. We will know tomorrow, if the Bills’ coaching staff agrees with me.

sports.body: This weekend, the Buffalo Bills square off against one of the franchise’s biggest foes, historically. In fact, some would say the Miami Dolphins are still Buffalo’s biggest rival. True or otherwise, to call Bills-Dolphins a heated rivalry at this juncture is doing more lip service to the past than the present. What is a fact is that Buffalo and Miami have alternated between lengthy spans of one-sided win streaks. Since the end of the 1980s, the Bills have largely had the Dolphins’ number. Sunday’s game at Highmark Stadium marks the 17th regular-season game for quarterback Josh Allen against Miami, a series that’s seen some of his most dominant play. Since Allen took over as QB1 in 2018, Buffalo is 14-3 against the Dolphins (including 1 playoff win). In 16 regular-season games, Allen has thrown for 4,256 yards with 42 touchdowns and nine interceptions, adding 703 rushing yards and another nine touchdowns on the ground. sports.title: Shane Steichen: Daniel Jones didn't ask to be released
sports.summary: The Colts abruptly released quarterback Daniel Jones on Friday.
sports.body:
“No, this was a decision that was just made for both, you know, the best interests of both parties ,” Steichen said, via James Boyd of The Athletic .

Steichen also explained the timing by saying, “It’s just where we’re at in our season. . . . That’s just the situation that we’re at right now.”

The situation was clear. Jones was going to be benched, in order to ensure that he won’t suffer an injury that will trigger a $10.51 million guarantee for 2027. If that had happened, he would have been asked to be cut. And they likely would have done it.

So they accelerated it. Skipped steps. Got to where they would have landed after doing the dance.

Steichen also said that, as expected, Anthony Richardson will become the starter.

So instead of squatting on Jones and not letting him play, Jones gets a chance to land with a contender as a backup. Likely on the practice squad, which would give him the ability to jump to an active roster if/when a starter gets injured.

sports.title: Colts' mismanagement continues with release of QB Daniel Jones
sports.summary: The Colts arguably mishandled the Jonathan Taylor situation, when it comes to the possibility of trading him.
sports.body:
He has played two games since the deadline came and went, and now he’s been cut . They should have seen it coming.

They cut him to avoid an injury that would have triggered a $10.51 million guarantee in 2027. A trade would have avoided that guarantee. And they would have gotten something.

Now? They get nothing. They’ll pay him $50 million for 11 games and have three wins to show for it.

The Vikings were interested, and they were talking to the Colts. While Minnesota wanted Kirk Cousins, the Colts could have lowered the price to a point that the Vikings couldn’t have refused.

Then again, the Vikings may have used the possibility of pivoting to Jones to get the Raiders down to a third-round pick for Cousins.

Regardless, the Colts blew it. It’s no surprise. They have no General Manager. Which makes it hard to generally manage the decisions that come with the opportunities to trade players.

Our guess is that the trades of guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner created the perception that the Colts were having a fire sale. Which resulted in lower offers for players like Taylor and Jones.

In the end, they traded neither. Now, Jones is gone. Taylor possibly will ask to be traded after the season, or they’ll decide to do it again on their own. Chances are that, when they do, they’ll get less than they could have gotten if they’d traded him at the deadline.

sports.title: Colts release QB Daniel Jones

sports.body:

Jones would have then asked to be released, and the Colts would have likely done it.

So the Colts went straight to the final move on the chess board.

Jones will, once officially released, go to waivers. If/when (when) he clears waivers, he’ll become a free agent.

In the early years, Miami dominated the rivalry, winning championships and making trips to the Super Bowl. Then came the Jim Kelly-Dan Marino era, when two future Hall of Fame quarterbacks battled for AFC supremacy. sports.body: Look what we have here, Rumblers: It’s a primetime matchup between a pair of AFC teams. Though we’ve had a couple this season and more frequently of late, AFC vs. AFC is about as rare as a Barbary lion these days. The trouble here is that this is a terrible matchup, featuring teams that are decidedly anything other than apex hunters. That the NFL can still sell this product to anyone is an incredible feat. Yet football fans continue lining up to see awful teams take on each other. It’s not that this one is without some interest, which is due to a few star players among both Houston and Indianapolis. The issue is that as Buffalo Bills fans, you’re settling in to watch the 3-6 Texans take on the 3-7 Colts. Those two teams are a combined 6-13 — which, if you’ve done the math, is less total wins than the 8-1 Bills have on the season. Neither of these teams was supposed to flop this season, though the writing was on the wall for Indianapolis. But Houston? It’s been an epic collapse for the Texans in 2026. A once-mighty defense has proven feckless far too often this season, which has some saying that head coach DeMeco Ryans could be warming the very seat he sits on in Houston. Fair or not, the NFL is a production-based industry. If you’re like me, the game will be on simply because it helps fill the room a bit this evening. You may also share my passion for the Thursday Night Football crew, and their pre-/postgame coverage. If nothing else, there’s also the chances to see the Texans in their Nike Rivals uniforms — and yes, they sure did again steal the Oilers’ vibe. Are you looking for a reason to root on one team over the other here? What you favor depends on who to cheer on to victory. A Houston win helps Buffalo’s strength of schedule/strength of victory, which matters most for NFL teams with postseason hopes on life support. Instead, you may prefer seeing the Colts win simply so it “harms” the slotting of 2027 first-round pick they sent to the New York Jets. With that, here’s your open thread for Week 11 of Thursday Night Football. Maybe this one also turns into a decent game, like a few suspect snooze-fests in primetime before it. As always, be kind to one another — and in all things… Go Bills!

sports.body: The Buffalo Bills announced that they will retire wide receiver Andre Reed’s No. 83 jersey at some point during the 2027 NFL season. While the team did not announce when it will happen, they did announce that it will happen, giving fans the news that the retirement ceremony will happen sometime during next season. [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBills/status/2123567003025784832?a=eiDWs2sPcy4ZrR46DXg&s=20] Reed is Buffalo’s franchise leader in targets (1,585), receptions (941), receiving yards (13,095), and receiving touchdowns (86). He played in Buffalo for 15 seasons, earning seven consecutive Pro Bowl nods from 1988-1994. He was named Second-Team All-Pro by the Associated Press in 1989 and 1990. A fourth-round draft choice out of Kutztown State University in Kutztown, PA, Reed was a key piece of a Buffalo team that made 10 playoff appearances, five AFC Championship Game appearances, and four Super Bowl appearances during his time with the franchise. At the time of his retirement, Reed ranked No. 3 all-time in receptions, and while he has since slipped to No. 23 all-time, it doesn’t dampen his accomplishments at all. A more pass-happy game has replaced the style of football played during Reed’s time in the league, making his numbers that much more impressive. Currently, Reed’s No. 83 jersey is worn by tight end Keleki Latu. Based on this announcement, it appears that Latu will need a new jersey number next year. Congratulations to Andre Reed—Go Bills! sports.body: The Buffalo Bills will play the Miami Dolphins on Sunday. The question right now is which Bills will actually play. Buffalo played their first of two straight divisional games last week and came back to Orchard Park with another win, but it may have cost them a significant portion of their roster. After a walkthrough practice on Wednesday, here’s what the Bills’ practice looked like today: [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBillsPR/status/2123529886702899498?a=q2z0msg8jWIlHqzpZ8g&s=20] Here’s What Changed * Dee Alford (concussion) - upgraded to Limited * Cole Bishop (shoulder) - upgraded to Full * Damar Hamlin (toe) - downgraded to DNP* * Jackson Hawes (shoulder) - downgraded to Limited* * T.J. Sanders (shoulder) - downgraded to Limited * O’Cyrus Torrence (personal) - returned to practice *On the report that Buffalo Bills PR published yesterday, Hamlin was listed as limited and Hawes was not listed at all. Today, the adjusted report shows today shows them as DNP and Limited respectively. Here’s What Stayed the Same * Christian Benford (groin) - DNP * Keon Coleman (ankle) - Full * Ray Davis (hamstring) - Limited * Amani Hooker (knee) - Limited * Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) - DNP * Ty Johnson (knee) - Full * Connor McGovern (neck) - Full * Tyrell Shavers (knee) - Full * Dorian Williams (calf) - DNP What We’re Watching The Bills defense is still looking thin despite the fact it looks as though Alford has progressed to the next step of the NFL’s concussion protocol. He will need a full practice on Friday and then no new symptoms on Saturday in order to completely clear the process and be ready to play. I would still look to see Tre’Davious White called up this weekend. The second practice squad elevation could go to Shaq Thompson. The veteran linebacker has been waiting for a game jersey this season, and with Williams not practicing for the second straight day, it looks like this could be the week. It’s also looking like the tight end room is struggling, but the Bills now have six wide receivers on the roster – plus they still have two more tight ends – so it’s doubtful they adjust much in their game plan.

sports.body: Have you ever gone to the therapist and they play that word association game? They will show you something, and they want you to use one word to describe it. In this case, we weren’t in a doctor’s office; we were in the New York Jets locker room. The one word ESPN’s Rich Cimini used to describe Geno Smith was “gimpy.” Smith did his media availability on Wednesday, November 18, “with a noticeable limp,” according to Cimini. The veteran QB said the “plan” is for him to be the QB1 on the road against the Los Angeles Chargers. Suboptimal. Smith wasn’t exactly fleet of foot at the ripe age of 36 when he was fully healthy. Now he’s got a bum wheel? This could lead to disastrous results in Week 11. Perhaps head coach Aaron Glenn is trying to pull a fast one on the Chargers by pretending that Smith is going to start, only to pull a last-second switch, and it’ll be rookie Cade Klubnik under center. I’m sure the Chargers are on pins and needles waiting to find out. The 2-8 Jets that have lost five in a row want to keep as much mystery going as possible to force Los Angeles to waste time preparing for multiple things. --- J-E-T-S!
